name: Calendar
description: Opens time on a resource a claim books: a stylist, a chair, a room, a collection counter, a pool of bikes. Weekly opening hours in an IANA time zone, which an instance may set for itself, less its closures, give the times a hold may take; capacity says how many holds may overlap. A claim takes time only through the supply contract's operations, which Holds invokes by name: holdFor holds an interval an item of the claim asks, commitFor books it for good and releaseFor frees it. Each checks the claim's own Holds.items, so no caller holds or frees time by calling one directly, and each is idempotent. holdFor refuses an interval outside the hours or in a closure, off the start grid, too short or too long, too soon or too far ahead by the engine's clock, or beyond capacity at any instant, buffers included. findAvailability answers free slots across the schema's instances by the same rules. Wall times become instants through a time zone database the engine carries, so every server built from one lock file computes the same slots; a wall time a daylight-saving change skips has no slot. An instance is not deleted while it holds time for a claim: time held, or committed and not yet ended. Calendar and Stock declare the same contract operations, so a type composes one of them.

capacity.description: How many holds may overlap at any instant: a count, or an own integer field of the type ({ field }) whose value of at least 1 is the instance's; 1 when absent.

field.description: An own integer field of the type, by JSON key.

slotMs.description: The start grid, in milliseconds: a hold starts a whole number of slots after an opening time. Any whole minute when absent.

minMs.description: The shortest hold, in milliseconds; slotMs when absent.

maxMs.description: The longest hold, in milliseconds; a day when absent.

bufferMs.description: Time kept free around each hold, which counts against capacity as the hold does.

before.description: Milliseconds before a hold that no other may overlap; 0 when absent.

after.description: Milliseconds after a hold that no other may overlap; 0 when absent.

leadMs.description: How long ahead of its start a hold must be made, by the engine's clock; 0 when absent.

horizonMs.description: How far ahead a hold may start, by the engine's clock; no limit when absent.

permission.description: The permission a caller needs to set an instance's hours and to add or remove its closures; a closure over held time needs its .override. Nobody may when absent.

fields.name: timeZone
fields.description: The time zone the instance's hours are in: its own when setOpeningHours set one, else the config's.

fields.name: closures
fields.description: The closures that have not ended, soonest first, at most 100: { closure, startMs, endMs, reason }.

operations.name: setOpeningHours
operations.description: Sets the instance's own weekly hours, its time zone, or both; null for either goes back to the config's. Holds already made stay; the time zone changes only while the instance holds no time that has not ended. Needs the config's permission.

hours.description: The instance's hours, or null for the config's.

oneOf.description: Opening hours by day of the week, mon to sun: each day a list of [open, close] wall-time ranges in the time zone, each closing after it opens, none overlapping. A day absent or empty is closed.

operations.name: addClosure
operations.description: Closes the instance from startMs to endMs, with a reason. Needs the config's permission; refused over time a claim holds unless force is set, which needs the permission's .override. Forcing keeps the holds: the claims are moved by their own Workflow, by a rule or by hand.

endMs.description: When it ends, after startMs, in epoch milliseconds.

startMs.description: When it starts, in epoch milliseconds.

endMs.description: When it ends, in epoch milliseconds.

operations.description: Removes a closure. Needs the config's permission.

operations.description: Holds what an item of a claim's Holds asks, for that claim, once the claim's item is held. Refused when it does not fit, and for an item the claim does not hold.

item.description: The item's index in its hold: its element's in an each hold's list, 0 for a link hold.

interval.description: The time the item asks, from startMs to endMs, in epoch milliseconds.

endMs.description: When it ends, after startMs and no later than 9000-01-01T00:00Z.

state.description: The item's state in this supply's record after the call.

changed.description: Whether the call moved the record; false for a call made again.

unitPrice.description: The unit price the item was held at, in the currency's minor units, when the supply names one.

operations.name: listBookings
operations.description: Lists the holds the instance has over a window of at most 31 days, by start, one page at a time: each claim's item, its interval and its state, held or committed.

startMs.description: The window's start, in epoch milliseconds.

endMs.description: The window's end, after startMs and at most 31 days after it.

limit.description: At most this many; 50 when absent.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

item.description: The item's index in its hold.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: findAvailability
operations.description: Finds free slots of a duration across the schema's instances over a window of at most 31 days, by holdFor's rules at the engine's clock: at most limit slots, soonest first, each with the instance and how many more holds it can take then. ids or where narrow the instances, as a list does.

startMs.description: The window's start, in epoch milliseconds.

endMs.description: The window's end, after startMs and at most 31 days after it.

durationMs.description: How long each slot is, in milliseconds.

where.description: Only the instances a list with this filter returns.

limit.description: At most this many slots; 100 when absent.

remaining.description: How many more holds the instance can take over the slot.

truncated.description: Whether more slots fit than limit returned, more instances matched than were read, or the search stopped at its bound of work.

vetoes.description: The claim the call names does not ask it: it has no such item for this supply, the item asks otherwise, or it is not in the state the call needs; or this supply's record of the item does not move that way.
